speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what is the Ministry's position with regard to healthcare institutions seeking external accreditations for continuous improvement; and (b) whether the Ministry is looking into coming up with more comprehensive and progressive audit standards like the Joint Commission International (JCI) to sustain Singapore's reputation of a world-class healthcare system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: These requirements are reviewed regularly to ensure they remain relevant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: At the systems level, MOH also benchmark the performance of our system against international counterparts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We examine how our care outcomes fare in international studies, such as the Economist Intelligence Unit's (EIU's) Healthcare Outcomes Index, Bloomberg's Global Health Index and the World Health Organization's World Health Statistics report.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We also benchmark ourselves in specific areas, such as our mortality rates in key diseases versus the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Singapore’s healthcare system has fared well in many of these international comparisons and studies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: In addition to these efforts, MOH encourages and supports quality improvements in healthcare institutions through different initiatives, such as performance monitoring and Quality Improvement programmes to help healthcare institutions achieve better care quality and excellence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Our healthcare landscape is rapidly changing, with emerging challenges in an ageing population, increased complexity of care needs and limited workforce growth.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Can I ask the Senior Minister of State when will be the timeline for implementation of this new audit system?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Currently, MOH is working with the National Quality Council and the clusters' Public Health Institutions to chart our way forward to ensure that there will be continued care quality and safety.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We are also engaging leading international organisations, including JCI as well as the Australian Council for Healthcare Standards (ACHS), to share some of the needs of the Singapore healthcare system, so that whatever suggestions that had been submitted to us actually meet our unique circumstances.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Once we have finalised the decision, we will update the House, as appropriate.
